title: Unit 10: Applied Grammar, Syntax & Advanced Idioms (SLO Essentials)
subject: english-12

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence that eliminates the error in comparative adjective usage:

options.A: He is more senior than me in the civil service.
options.B: He is senior to me in the civil service.
options.C: He is senior than I in the civil service.
options.D: He is most senior to me in the civil service.

questions.explanation: Latin-derived adjectives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take the preposition 'to', never 'than' or 'more'.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that uses the correct preposition of dying:

options.A: The brave soldier died from cholera in the trenches.
options.B: The brave soldier died of cholera in the trenches.
options.C: The brave soldier died with cholera in the trenches.
options.D: The brave soldier died by cholera in the trenches.

questions.explanation: One dies 'of' a specific disease (cancer, cholera, fever), dies 'from' an external cause (wounds, exhaustion), and dies 'for' a noble cause.

questions.question: Choose the correct version of the sentence containing the indefinite pronoun 'one':

options.A: One must do his duty honestly at all times.
options.B: One must do one's duty honestly at all times.
options.C: One must do their duty honestly at all times.
options.D: One must do her duty honestly at all times.

questions.explanation: The pronoun 'one' must maintain consistency throughout the sentence; its possessive form is strictly 'one's'.

questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence concerning preference:

options.A: I prefer tea than coffee in the evening.
options.B: I prefer tea to coffee in the evening.
options.C: I prefer tea more than coffee in the evening.
options.D: I prefer tea over to coffee in the evening.

questions.explanation: The verb 'prefer' takes the preposition 'to' when comparing two nouns or gerunds ('prefer X to Y').

questions.question: Identify the correct negative construction:

options.A: Both boys did not attend the lecture.
options.B: Neither of the boys attended the lecture.
options.C: Both did not went to the lecture.
options.D: Neither boy did not attend the lecture.

questions.explanation: Standard English avoids using 'both' in negative sentences; 'neither of the two' is the proper grammatical phrasing.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding uncountable nouns:

options.A: The professor gave me many useful advices.
options.B: The professor gave me many useful pieces of advice.
options.C: The professor gave me an advice.
options.D: The professor gave me advices.

questions.explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun with no plural 'advices'; pluralization requires a partitive counter ('pieces of advice').

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct subject-verb inversion following a negative adverbial?

options.A: Seldom I have witnessed such extraordinary heroism.
options.B: Seldom have I witnessed such extraordinary heroism.
options.C: Seldom I witnessed such extraordinary heroism.
options.D: Seldom had I witness such extraordinary heroism.

questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with a restrictive or negative adverb (seldom, rarely, never, hardly), the auxiliary verb precedes the subject.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'a white elephant'?

options.A: A rare albino animal in an Asian sanctuary
options.B: A possession that is useless, burdensome, and extremely expensive to maintain
options.C: An enormous unexpected financial profit
options.D: A wise elder statesman

questions.explanation: 'A white elephant' refers to a costly possession whose maintenance exceeds its usefulness.

questions.question: Identify the sentence with the correct use of 'lest':

options.A: Walk carefully lest you should stumble on the rocks.
options.B: Walk carefully lest you may not stumble on the rocks.
options.C: Walk carefully lest you will stumble on the rocks.
options.D: Walk carefully lest you stumble not on the rocks.

questions.explanation: 'Lest' inherently contains a negative meaning ('for fear that') and takes the modal auxiliary 'should' without 'not'.

questions.question: Choose the correct idiom meaning 'to face an unexpected, shocking calamity':

options.A: A bolt from the blue
options.B: A storm in a teacup
options.C: Barking up the wrong tree
options.D: Crying over spilt milk

questions.explanation: 'A bolt from the blue' describes a sudden, completely unexpected and shocking catastrophe.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence:

options.A: Ten miles are a long distance to walk on foot.
options.B: Ten miles is a long distance to walk on foot.
options.C: Ten miles were a long distance to walk on foot.
options.D: Ten mile is a long distance to walk on foot.

questions.explanation: Expressions of distance, time, and money are treated as single collective units of measurement and take singular verbs ('is').

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The candidate was absorbed _____ deep philosophical reflection.'

options.A: in
options.B: at
options.C: with
options.D: upon

questions.explanation: The adjective 'absorbed' takes the preposition 'in' when describing mental concentration or immersion.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to leave no stone unturned' mean?

options.A: To do heavy construction work
options.B: To try every possible course of action or exhaust every method to achieve an objective
options.C: To throw rocks into a river
options.D: To search for gemstones in a quarry

questions.explanation: Leaving no stone unturned means exploring every conceivable avenue or strategy to accomplish a goal.

questions.question: Choose the correct Third Conditional sentence:

options.A: If you worked hard, you will pass.
options.B: If you had worked hard, you would have passed the examination.
options.C: If you work hard, you would have passed.
options.D: If you had worked hard, you will have passed.

questions.explanation: The Third Conditional expresses past counterfactuals: 'If + past perfect ... would have + past participle'.

questions.question: Identify the sentence that eliminates the dangling modifier:

options.A: Walking along the canal, the moon rose beautifully.
options.B: While I was walking along the canal, the moon rose beautifully.
options.C: Walking along the canal, beautiful was the moon.
options.D: Having walked along the canal, the moon was rising.

questions.explanation: The moon cannot walk along the canal; introducing the subject 'I' resolves the dangling participle.

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect form of: The teacher said to the boys, 'Do not make a noise.'

options.A: The teacher forbade the boys to make a noise.
options.B: The teacher forbade the boys not to make a noise.
options.C: The teacher said to the boys that they should not make noise.
options.D: The teacher told the boys to not make a noise.

questions.explanation: The verb 'forbade' already contains a negative meaning, so adding 'not' would create an erroneous double negative.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'to burn the candle at both ends'?

options.A: To light two candles during a blackout
options.B: To exhaust oneself by working late into the night and rising early, overtaxing one's physical energy
options.C: To waste paraffin wax carelessly
options.D: To celebrate a birthday

questions.explanation: Burning the candle at both ends means exhausting one's physical and mental resources through excessive, relentless labor.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'Pasteur was exempt _____ military service due to paralysis.'

options.A: from
options.B: with
options.C: at
options.D: for

questions.explanation: The adjective 'exempt' requires the preposition 'from'.

questions.question: Identify the correct sentence regarding collective nouns:

options.A: The jury has reached its verdict unanimously.
options.B: The jury have reached its verdict unanimously.
options.C: The jury has reached their verdict unanimously.
options.D: The juries has reached its verdict.

questions.explanation: When a collective noun acts as a unified body, it takes a singular verb ('has') and a singular pronoun ('its').

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'a feather in one's cap'?

options.A: An achievement or honor of which one can be justly proud
options.B: A bird hunting decoration
options.C: An act of cowardice
options.D: A light woolen hat

questions.explanation: 'A feather in one's cap' is a distinguished achievement or honor that brings credit to someone.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: He told me that the sun rose in the east.
options.B: He told me that the sun rises in the east.
options.C: He told me that the sun had risen in the east.
options.D: He told me that the sun would rise in the east.

questions.explanation: Universal scientific truths and eternal facts do not backshift their tense in indirect speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The student was accused _____ stealing the library manuscript.'

options.A: of
options.B: with
options.C: for
options.D: about

questions.explanation: The verb 'accuse' takes 'of' (accused of a crime), whereas 'charge' takes 'with'.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to take to task' mean?

options.A: To assign school homework
options.B: To reprimand, scold, or severely criticize someone for a blunder
options.C: To employ someone for wages
options.D: To complete a test quickly

questions.explanation: 'Taking someone to task' means rebuking or reprimanding them sternly for wrongdoing.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly utilizes the correlative conjunction 'not only ... but also'?

options.A: He not only visited the hospital, but also the library.
options.B: He visited not only the hospital but also the library.
options.C: Not only he visited the hospital, but the library.
options.D: He visited the hospital, but also not only the library.

questions.explanation: Parallelism demands that 'not only' and 'but also' introduce grammatically identical elements (both precede nouns: 'the hospital' and 'the library').

questions.question: What is the meaning of the idiom 'once in a blue moon'?

options.A: Every full moon night
options.B: Extremely rarely or almost never
options.C: During an astronomical eclipse
options.D: Every Monday morning

questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' is an established idiom for an event that occurs very infrequently.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: The sceneries of Murree are breathtaking.
options.B: The scenery of Murree is breathtaking.
options.C: The sceneries of Murree is breathtaking.
options.D: A scenery of Murree are breathtaking.

questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun with no plural form; it takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'She is proficient _____ English syntax and rhetoric.'

options.A: in
options.B: at
options.C: with
options.D: on

questions.explanation: One is proficient 'in' a subject, language, or field of knowledge.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to hit below the belt' mean?

options.A: To act in an unfair, treacherous, or cowardly manner
options.B: To score a goal in football
options.C: To fasten a leather belt tightly
options.D: To wear sports padding

questions.explanation: Derived from boxing rules, hitting below the belt means striking an opponent unfairly or dishonorably.

questions.question: Identify the passive form of: 'They will have finished the bridge by December.'

options.A: The bridge will have finished by them by December.
options.B: The bridge will have been finished by them by December.
options.C: The bridge will be finished by December.
options.D: The bridge would have finished by them by December.

questions.explanation: Future perfect passive requires 'will have been + past participle' ('will have been finished').

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to smell a rat' signify?

options.A: To detect an unpleasant odor in a cellar
options.B: To suspect deception, treachery, or foul play
options.C: To keep pet rodents
options.D: To set a mousetrap

questions.explanation: 'To smell a rat' means to have an intuitive suspicion that something dishonest or deceptive is occurring.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:

options.A: If I was you, I would consult Dr. Merivale immediately.
options.B: If I were you, I would consult Dr. Merivale immediately.
options.C: If I am you, I will consult Dr. Merivale.
options.D: If I had been you, I will consult Dr. Merivale.

questions.explanation: Hypothetical contrary-to-fact conditions require the subjunctive 'were' regardless of the subject pronoun.

questions.question: Choose the correct preposition: 'The headmaster concurred _____ the decision of the governors.'

options.A: with
options.B: at
options.C: to
options.D: against

questions.explanation: One concurs 'with' a person or decision, meaning to agree or share an opinion.

questions.question: What does the idiom 'to nip in the bud' mean?

options.A: To prune rose gardens in spring
options.B: To stop or destroy a problem in its earliest nascent stage before it can develop
options.C: To pick flowers before blooming
options.D: To water houseplants

questions.explanation: 'To nip in the bud' means to extinguish a difficulty or vice at the very beginning before it takes root.

questions.question: Choose the correctly constructed sentence:

options.A: He ran as fastly as he could.
options.B: He ran as fast as he could.
options.C: He ran more fastly than anyone.
options.D: He ran as faster as possible.

questions.explanation: 'Fast' is both an adjective and an adverb; the word 'fastly' does not exist in standard English.

questions.question: What is the primary SLO requirement for the FBISE Section A English paper?

options.A: Rote memorization of textbook exercise questions without context
options.B: Demonstrating conceptual comprehension of prescribed texts and applying rigorous rules of functional grammar, syntax, and rhetoric
options.C: Translating whole pages into classical Greek
options.D: Writing personal diaries during examination hours

questions.explanation: The Federal Board SLO framework evaluates analytical understanding of literary themes and practical application of standard English grammar.
